clearedSpotChecks.check: Arc: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source, with native USDC legs summed from the system emitter 0xffff...fffe Transfer logs (162 native legs exact, 12 of them in blocks with other PoolManager transactions).
clearedSpotChecks.note: The Arc page https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/usdc-system-events.md was fetched in this session. It says the system emitter logs a Transfer at 18 decimals for every native value transfer (CALL, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT) and for the precompile mint, burn and transfer behind the ERC-20 face. I tested the emitter as a full account of the PoolManager balance. For blocks 32876998, 32790538, 32788980 and 32774115 (four of the twelve where the balance difference had disagreed) and 32908380, I summed every emitter Transfer to and from the PoolManager 0x8366a39c... in the whole block from rpc.mainnet.arc.io. Each sum equals eth_getBalance(block) minus eth_getBalance(block-1) to the wei. The emitter logs are written by block production, so attributing native legs per transaction with them is sound. The twelve earlier disagreements came from other transactions in the same block and do not hide an over-payment. The owed side follows src/libraries/Pool.sol:205-235, src/libraries/Position.sol:84-100 and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:188-211,234-254 as I read them. The rounding of getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta for a negative delta is false, which is what analyze2.py's amounts() and v4math use. One residual is that a transaction with both a native leg and a 0x3600... ERC-20 USDC leg would produce emitter logs for both legs. None of the 162 transactions disagreed, so no case of this kind affected the result.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source, 169 transactions exact, native legs from debug_traceTransaction and the PoolManager balance difference.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The payment result holds. I reran analyze2.py's one() on 0x401d3343... (block 125003198) and 0x62289cf7... (block 125009634) against rpc3/rpc1/monadinfra. Both came out exact with no storage mismatch, and for the first one the balance difference equals the traced native payment. The supporting count in the cleared text is wrong. raw/an2-143.json and raw/an2-143b.json hold 108 native legs: 69 are alone in their block and all 69 agree with the balance difference, 18 in shared blocks also agree, and 21 in shared blocks differ because other transactions moved native value. The text says 87 alone in their block, all agreeing. The correct numbers are 87 agreeing, 69 alone. So 39 Monad native legs rest only on the RPC node's re-execution in debug_traceTransaction, with no block-production record. Of the 108 native legs, 92 paid a nonzero amount, not 108. Monad full nodes execute every block with the same client as validators, which makes a split between trace and production unlikely. That point is inferred and I did not confirm it from a fetched source. The bitmap words written by flipTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:175-180) are not part of the storage comparison in analyze2.py verify(); only tick info, positions, slot0 and liquidity are.

clearedSpotChecks.check: MegaETH: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source, 413 transactions exact, 287 native legs each alone in its block with the balance difference equal to the traced payment.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran analyze2.py's one() on the collection 0xb8d0f150... (block 32646241) at mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc. It came out exact with no storage mismatch. The ERC-20 leg of 11530006929321746558 units was paid exactly and the native leg was zero, with balance difference 0. In raw/an3-4326.json all 287 native legs are alone in their block, matching totals.json. Of these, 244 paid a nonzero native amount, so the 287 counts zero legs as well. The balance and the receipt logs come from what the sequencer's executor wrote (F-118), so the 244 nonzero native legs and all ERC-20 legs are checked against production output. The parent-block storage comes from the RPC replica's state, and I did not confirm independently that this state equals what the sequencer wrote. The match between predicted and post-block storage in all 413 transactions supports it. The transcription follows src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-237 and 488-557 as I read them, including the order of updateTick, getFeeGrowthInside, Position.update and clearTick.
